recognize_zh: 周邊血液中出現一顆漿細胞：核圓而偏於一側、染色質粗顆粒，細胞質豐富深藍並有明顯核旁淡染區（perinuclear hof），背景紅血球有數顆堆疊的輕度錢串狀排列，符合骨髓瘤病人血中的循環漿細胞。
features: Single plasma cell, about 2 times the size of a red cell
Round, eccentric nucleus with coarse clumped chromatin; no conspicuous nucleolus
Abundant deeply basophilic cytoplasm with prominent perinuclear hof and fine cytoplasmic vacuolation
Background red cells with short stacks of 2-4 cells suggesting mild rouleaux formation
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a circulating plasma cell with an eccentric round nucleus, coarse clumped chromatin, and abundant deeply basophilic, finely vacuolated cytoplasm with a distinct perinuclear hof. Background red cells show short stacks suggestive of mild rouleaux formation, and platelets are unremarkable. A single circulating plasma cell does not by itself establish plasma cell leukemia; the absolute and percentage count of circulating plasma cells (≥5% defines plasma cell leukemia per current criteria) should be determined. In a patient with known multiple myeloma, findings are consistent with circulating neoplastic plasma cells.

ddx.vs: Reactive plasmacytoid lymphocytes are part of a heterogeneous reactive lymphocytosis with less distinct hofs, and they are polytypic on flow cytometry.
LPL shows circulating small lymphocytes and plasmacytoid lymphocytes with IgM paraprotein and MYD88 L265P, rather than a mature plasma cell in a myeloma patient.
Morphology is identical; plasma cell leukemia requires ≥5% circulating clonal plasma cells on the differential count.
Basophilic normoblasts have a central round nucleus with dense chromatin and uniformly blue cytoplasm without a perinuclear hof.
